hints: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. Distance is the area under v from 0 to T.
worded:
1. v is never negative, so distance = area under ½kt² from 0 to T = kT³/6.

2. Dividing by T gives kT²/6. (D)

3. Sense check: the average of t² over 0 to T is T²/3 (not T²/2, because the curve is low for most of the time). Then ½k × T²/3 = kT²/6.
mistakes: Averaging the first and last speeds (½ × ½kT² = ¼kT²) works only for constant acceleration; here a is not constant.
